title: Test bounded retries without waiting
sources: Python 3.14 Standard Library: unittest.mock side_effect iterable and call_count
masterChecklist: Unit, integration, end-to-end, regression, property-based, and contract-test concepts
unittest, unittest.mock, test doubles, patching namespaces correctly
Automation and scripting: files, APIs, browser/task automation concepts, scheduling, resilience
whyItMatters: A temporary failure may deserve one more attempt, but uncontrolled retries can repeat work forever or make tests painfully slow.
simpleExplanation: A retry helper calls an action up to a fixed number of attempts. It catches only a chosen temporary error, such as TimeoutError. Between attempts it calls a sleeper function passed in by the caller. Production may use time.sleep; a test passes a Mock, so no real time passes. Mock(side_effect=[TimeoutError('temporary'), 'ok']) makes the first call fail and the second succeed. Retrying is safe only when repeating the action cannot cause harmful duplicates, or when the operation has an appropriate idempotency design.
mentalModel: A delivery worker may try again after a temporary closed door, but stops after a set number of knocks and never claims delivery before it succeeds.
outcomes: Set a finite attempt count and validate it.
Retry only TimeoutError in this exercise.
Inject sleep to test without waiting.
Verify the attempt and sleep counts on success and exhaustion.

realWorldExample.scenario: The study platform reads a progress snapshot from a transiently unavailable service.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: An endless retry stalls the page, while retrying a non-idempotent submission could create duplicates.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Apply a bounded retry only to a safe read, expose the final timeout, and test first-failure-then-success plus exhaustion without a real network or timer.

explanation: The attempt limit is checked before any call.
The loop counts at most three calls to read.
TimeoutError is retried; another exception would propagate unchanged.
sleep runs only when another attempt remains.
The mock sequence produces a timeout then a successful result; the mock sleeper records a call but does not wait.

Define a positive maximum number of attempts.

commonMistakes.why: A programming bug or permanent rejection will repeat pointlessly.
commonMistakes.avoid: Catch only a documented transient failure.

commonMistakes.why: No later attempt will happen, so the delay only slows failure reporting.
commonMistakes.avoid: Re-raise immediately when the last attempt fails.

commonMistakes.mistake: Retrying a write without checking duplicate effects.
commonMistakes.why: The first attempt might have succeeded remotely even if the response timed out.
commonMistakes.avoid: Use this helper for safe reads; design idempotency separately for writes.

lab.title: Retry a safe read with no real delay
lab.safety: Mocks simulate the read and pause; no network or real waiting is required. The in-site Run Python button executes this lab in a fresh browser worker; this particular exercise uses neither local computer files nor external services.
lab.starterCode:
from unittest.mock import Mock

def retry_read(read, sleep, attempts=3):
    # Validate attempts. Retry TimeoutError only.
    pass

# Test temporary failure followed by success and repeated failure.
guidedSteps: Raise ValueError when attempts is below one.
Loop over range(attempts) and return read() on success.
Catch TimeoutError and re-raise on the final attempt.
Call sleep(1) only before another attempt.
Use a second mock that always times out to prove exhaustion and no last sleep.
checks: Recovery returns ready after two reads and one sleep.
All-timeout case raises after the configured number of attempts.
No sleep occurs after the final failure.
An unrelated ValueError is not retried.
lab.solutionExplanation: The mocks prove the precise number of attempts and pauses without a real timer. The final timeout is visible, and a different failure is not retried.
challenges: Predict the sleep count when every attempt fails with attempts=3.
Find the bug: catch Exception instead of TimeoutError.
Experiment with attempts=1 and verify the sleeper is never called.

simulation.prompt: Which operation is safest for this introductory retry helper?
choices: A read with no side effects
A payment submission with no duplicate protection
simulation.explanation: A read is safe to repeat; a write may create duplicate effects.

lab.testCode:
read=Mock(side_effect=[TimeoutError('temporary'),'ready']); sleep=Mock()
assert retry_read(read,sleep)=='ready'
assert read.call_count==2
sleep.assert_called_once_with(1)
wrong=Mock(side_effect=ValueError('bad'))
try: retry_read(wrong,Mock())
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError('permanent error retried')
assert wrong.call_count==1
print('PASS: bounded injected retry')

projectConnection.milestone: Add a bounded retry to a safe progress read and test recovery and exhaustion with injected mocks.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: The read has finite attempts, retries only TimeoutError, never sleeps after its final failure, and tests run without network or real delay.

assessment.question: Why inject a sleeper function?
assessment.answer: Tests can observe pause calls without waiting in real time.
assessment.explanation: It removes timing as a source of slow or flaky tests.

assessment.question: What happens on the final TimeoutError?
assessment.answer: It is re-raised without another sleep.

assessment.question: Why not blindly retry a submission write?
assessment.answer: A timeout may occur after the remote write succeeded, making a retry duplicate it.
assessment.explanation: Write retries need a deliberate idempotency design.
